facts.raw_span: eruption on his trunk that began 2 months previously with multiple round red patches slowly increasing in size
neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and juvenile xanthogranulomas
Treatment with griseofulvin and clotrimazole had not improved the rash
developed fever and was diagnosed with otitis media
Multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale ranging from 1 to 6 cm in diameter on his trunk
Scattered café au lait macules present on the back
Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm
Immunohistochemical staining: Positive: CD33, CD123, CD4, CD163
White blood cell count: 76,400/µL
Annular dusky red indurated plaques on right flank and back with central clearing and trailing scale, scattered café au lait macules
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showing perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate (×40 and ×400 magnification)
No family history of NF1

concepts.why: The presence of perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, positive immunohistochemical staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163, and a high white blood cell count are consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis, particularly in a patient with a history of neurofibromatosis type 1.
The patient's history of juvenile xanthogranuloma and the presence of multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale are consistent with this diagnosis.

The presence of multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale, and scattered café au lait macules, could be consistent with mastocytosis, although the immunohistochemical staining results do not support this diagnosis as strongly as they do Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

The perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, and the high white blood cell count, could be consistent with leukemia cutis, although the clinical presentation and immunohistochemical staining results are more suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

The presence of perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, and the high white blood cell count, could be consistent with histiocytic sarcoma, although the clinical presentation and immunohistochemical staining results are more suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The histopathology finding of perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate with positive CD33, CD123, and CD4 staining is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
